claim: German food rationing by card from 28 August 1939, graded by occupation (heavy and very heavy workers drew supplements); the Reich clothing card (points) from November 1939.
source: Standard histories of the German home front; not re-read against a source in this round.

claim: Goebbels' Sportpalast speech, 18 February 1943; the decree of 27 January 1943 requiring men and women not in work to register for war labour; millions of foreign civilian workers, many deported, and prisoners of war in German industry and farming.
source: Standard histories; not re-read against a source in this round.

claim: Decree of 26 June 1940: eight-hour day, seven-day week, no leaving a job without permission, lateness over twenty minutes a criminal offence; well over a million convictions in its first year, mostly corrective labour at the workplace with pay deducted.
source: Standard histories of Soviet labour law; the conviction count is given as a floor (more than a million).

claim: Rationing from July 1941 in Moscow and Leningrad, extended to other towns; categories by work (war industry highest, dependants and children lowest); collective farm markets at far higher prices; women, teenagers and the old in evacuated industry, long shifts.
source: Standard histories; not re-read against a source in this round.

claim: British rationing from 8 January 1940 (bacon, butter, sugar), meat from March 1940; registration with retailers; many evacuated children back home during the phoney war; more road deaths in the blackout than deaths from enemy action in late 1939.
source: Standard histories of the British home front.

claim: Eden's broadcast of 14 May 1940 calling for Local Defence Volunteers; the Emergency Powers (Defence) Act 1940 passed on 22 May 1940 in one day; signposts removed from late May 1940.
source: Standard histories; the volunteer count is given only as hundreds of thousands within days.

claim: Italian bread rationing from October 1941 at about 200 grams a day; pasta, oil and sugar rationed before it; coffee substitutes; prefects' reports on public opinion.
source: Standard histories of the Italian home front; the ration is given as about 200 grams.

claim: Strikes from 5 March 1943 at Fiat Mirafiori, Turin, spreading to Milan; demands included the bombing allowance for all workers; first mass strikes in Axis Europe.
source: Standard histories of the March 1943 strikes.

claim: Rice rationing in the six largest cities from April 1941 at 2.3 go (about 330 g) a day for an adult; passbooks; neighbourhood associations; sugar and matches rationed in 1940; National Mobilisation Law 1938.
source: Standard histories of the Japanese home front.

claim: Group evacuation of schoolchildren from the large cities from August 1944, hundreds of thousands, to temples and inns; B-29s from the Marianas from November 1944.
source: Standard histories; the number is given only as hundreds of thousands.

claim: Last civilian cars built February 1942; tyre rationing from the first weeks after Pearl Harbor; sugar rationing May 1942; petrol rationing on the East Coast May 1942; the War Production Board, January 1942.
source: Standard histories of the American home front.

claim: More than six million women joined the paid labour force during the war; Executive Order 8802 of 25 June 1941 forbade discrimination in defence industry; the wartime migration of Black workers north and west and the housing shortage.
source: Standard histories; the number of women is given as a floor (more than six million).
